texts: bad: 'the first cold snap of Year 2' comes out as a bare rank-1 ordinal with no slot for the 'of Year 2' domain, so the parse claims this was the first cold snap ever — wider than what you wrote. Split the ranking off into its own finite clause: 'On day 395 of Year 2, a cold snap came. No cold snap came in Year 2 before day 395.' Separately, note that 'day 395' lands in a day-of-month slot, so a 395th day of a year has no defined reading in the calendar the translator knows.

good. the every-lantern universal comes out as a fireable rule — a plain-variable premise on 'lantern' plus the 'on the Cliff Path' restriction — with the lantern's own mire-essence, the 'already' tag and past tense all carried.
good. 'no lantern' gives a strength-0 rule over lanterns with the 'no' quantifier word recorded alongside, and the phrasal 'went out' is kept whole.

bad: the per-station rule hands all three stations the one same portion of mire-essence, so the parse says the three stations burned a single shared portion rather than each its own. Make the per-station portion explicit: 'Each of the three bright stations burned its own extra mire-essence.'

bad: the same shared-witness problem as the burning clause — the per-station rule gives all three stations the very same mist-light, asserting they produced one and the same light. Since sentence 6's 'The strong mist-light' reads as one glow, mark this one collective: 'Together, the three bright stations produced strong mist-light.' That drops the per-station rule entirely and leaves exactly one mist-light for sentence 6 to refer back to.

bad: 'crowds of nightmoths' collapses into a single crowd, because a group whose members are themselves crowds has no licensed form — so the parse asserts one crowd where you wrote several. Use the singular collective the rest of the passage already uses, distributed over the stations: 'The strong mist-light attracted a crowd of nightmoths at each bright station.'

bad: two pieces have no carrier — 'about thirty' puts a hedged value in a count slot that takes a plain whole number, and 'per night' is read as how often the counting recurred rather than as a rate on the moths. State an exact count and a plain nightly recurrence: 'Each night, keepers counted thirty nightmoths at each bright station.' The 'about' hedge cannot be kept as a hedge — either drop it or state a bound instead ('at least twenty-five nightmoths').

bad: 'on six of the next ten nights' asks the parser to spread one gathering over a counted set of nights, but nights are time expressions rather than countable things, so the parse ends up with a single gather event holding a six-night group in its time slot — one occurrence where you wrote six, and sentences 9 to 11 then hang off that one collapsed event. There is no licensed form for a counted subset of nights: state the pattern instead — 'Each night, a crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row.' — or give each night its own dated sentence if exactly six is what matters.

mixed: the descent itself is fine, but 'on those six nights' inherits sentence 8's unencodable night set (one descend event standing in for six). Mirror whatever sentence 8 becomes: 'Each night, sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.' Also, the compound 'sky-cat' was minted without its 'a sky-cat is a cat' genus atom, unlike every other compound in the passage — that one is a translator slip and no rewrite of yours would change it.

mixed: the same six-nights collapse as sentence 9, so rewrite the time the same way: 'Each night, the sky-cats hunted nightmoths at the Middle Row.' The hunted nightmoths were also given the change-undergoing object role when hunting neither creates, destroys nor changes them — a translator-side role slip, not a problem with your wording.

bad: 'the hunts' is plural but there is only one hunt event in the parse for it to resolve to, so the plurality is silently lost. Tie the molting to the hunting with a finite clause instead of a plural definite: 'The sky-cats molted while they hunted.'
good. the feather group, the fall to the base of the cliff (with the base linked to the cliff as a part of it) and the per-feather distribution are all carried.
good. the strong-harvest state is reified and anchored one month after the feather fall, with the plain 'the harvest was strong' form kept alongside so a direct question still resolves.
